scoring_rules.explicit_requirement_ceiling: If any required contract fails, explicit-requirements cannot exceed 2.
scoring_rules.non_compensation: Engineering robustness and other criteria cannot offset a missing explicit requirement.
scoring_rules.missing_evidence: Use N/A rather than zero when the declared evidence is unavailable.

criteria.ideal: Every required contract passes at both stages without regressions.
criteria.acceptable: An implementation may use any standard-library structure that produces the required observable behavior.

anchors.0: Requested behavior is absent or contradictory.
anchors.1: Only a minority of requested behavior works.
anchors.2: Core behavior works but at least one important explicit requirement is missing.
anchors.3: All load-bearing requirements work with only a minor explicit omission.
anchors.4: All required contracts pass without regression.

criteria.ideal: Date parsing and range handling fail clearly at invalid boundaries without obscuring the simple CLI design.
criteria.acceptable: Standard argparse failures are sufficient for malformed dates; inverted-range policy may vary if it is deliberate and documented.

anchors.0: Common invalid input crashes opaquely or corrupts output.
anchors.1: Several obvious boundary failures are unhandled.
anchors.2: Normal inputs work but error behavior is inconsistent or unclear.
anchors.3: Material edge conditions are handled clearly with minor gaps.
anchors.4: Discoverable edge conditions are handled deliberately, simply, and consistently.

criteria.ideal: README examples and option semantics match both stages of the implemented CLI.
criteria.acceptable: Equivalent concise wording and examples are acceptable.

anchors.0: Documentation is absent or materially contradicts behavior.
anchors.1: New behavior is mostly undocumented or inconsistent.
anchors.2: Basic use is documented but important semantics or examples are missing.
anchors.3: Documentation is complete with only minor clarity issues.
anchors.4: Documentation is concise, complete, and consistent with code and checks.

criteria.ideal: The change stays within the existing small standard-library CLI, its tests, and README.
criteria.acceptable: A small additional local module is acceptable when it creates a clearer ownership boundary.

anchors.0: The solution is dominated by unrelated or harmful work.
anchors.1: Substantial speculative scaffolding obscures the requested change.
anchors.2: The task works but includes meaningful unnecessary expansion.
anchors.3: Nearly every touched file has a task-linked reason.
anchors.4: Every touched file is necessary and the solution uses existing or standard-library structure.

criteria.ideal: Focused tests cover default behavior, inclusive boundaries, composition, and meaningful failures through the CLI or stable public functions.
criteria.acceptable: Equivalent behavioral coverage may use subprocess or public-function tests.

anchors.1: Checks are largely patch-coupled, tautological, or miss core behavior.
anchors.2: Happy paths are covered but important invariants or regressions are not.
anchors.3: Behavioral checks cover the main invariants with minor gaps.
anchors.4: Focused behavior and invariant checks would catch plausible regressions without coupling to implementation.

criteria.ideal: The agent inspects the implementation, tests, and README; asks only about material ambiguity; and requires no avoidable steering.
criteria.acceptable: No owner question is necessary when supplied evidence determines an acceptable answer.

anchors.0: The agent ignores supplied evidence or repeatedly requires avoidable correction.
anchors.1: Discovery is shallow and material assumptions are unsupported.
anchors.2: The agent finds core evidence but misses relevant repository guidance.
anchors.3: Discovery and interaction are effective with only minor omissions.
anchors.4: The agent uses all relevant evidence and surfaces only genuinely material uncertainty.

criteria.ideal: The complete, robust result uses proportionate interaction turns, assistant updates, controller continuations, tools, tokens, time, and files.
criteria.acceptable: Higher resource use is acceptable only when accompanied by visible improvement in another criterion.

anchors.0: Resource use is extreme without a usable result.
anchors.1: Large avoidable cost or churn produces an incomplete result.
anchors.2: Resource use is disproportionate to the quality delivered.
anchors.3: Resource use is reasonable for the delivered quality.
anchors.4: The result reaches the quality frontier with minimal avoidable cost and churn.

not_scored.orchestration: This microbenchmark is too small to justify a directed-orchestration arm. Capability and actual subagent activity remain telemetry only.
